Heritage walk in Bengaluru: the pete, Tipu's palace and Cubbon Park

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

A heritage walk in Bengaluru (Bangalore) usually covers the old market town or pete founded by Kempe Gowda in 1537, the fort and Tipu Sultan's summer palace, the temples of Basavanagudi, and the colonial civic centre around Cubbon Park, with the Government Museum and Vidhana Soudha. Each area is a two to three hour walk; a vehicle links them.

We arrange Bengaluru heritage walks on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, led by an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi, with other languages through partners.

Why Bengaluru matters for heritage

Bengaluru is better known for software than for monuments, which is exactly why a heritage walk surprises people. The city has a clear sequence: a 16th century market town laid out by Kempe Gowda I, a chieftain under the Vijayanagara kings; a fort rebuilt in stone under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan; a British cantonment from 1809; and a 20th century state capital. Inscriptions found around the city, such as the Begur inscription of about the 9th to 10th century, show that the area was settled long before 1537.

Because the city has grown so fast, its heritage sits among flyovers and markets. That makes it a good place to talk about urban change, and a lecture such as Who owns the past? Heritage and urban development fits well with a walk here.

Historical places in Bengaluru by period

Kempe Gowda's town was a grid of petes (market streets) for different trades, such as Chickpet, Balepet and Cottonpet, which still carry those names. Older temples such as the Someshwara Temple at Halasuru, of Chola origin and expanded under Vijayanagara rule, and the cave temple of Gavi Gangadhareshwara survive from before or around his time. The four watchtowers credited to Kempe Gowda are later in their present form.

Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan turned Bengaluru into a military base and built the stone fort and Tipu's summer palace, finished in 1791. The British took the fort in 1791 during the Third Anglo-Mysore War. After 1831 the British ruled Mysore directly for fifty years, and their cantonment and civic buildings, such as the Attara Kacheri (1868), now the Karnataka High Court, date from this time. Vidhana Soudha, completed in 1956, belongs to the new state.

Places a heritage walk in Bengaluru covers

  1. Bangalore Fort Mud fort 1537, stone fort 18th century

    Only a gateway and some walls survive near KR Market. A plaque records the British assault of 1791.

  2. Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace Completed 1791

    Two-storey palace of teak with painted arches and pillars. A small display covers the Mysore wars.

  3. Kote Venkataramana Temple About 1689

    Dravida-style temple built under the Wodeyars beside the palace.

  4. Chickpet and Avenue Road 16th century onwards

    The core of Kempe Gowda's market grid, still a wholesale centre. Look at the old houses above the shops.

  5. Bull Temple 16th century

    Large monolithic Nandi in Basavanagudi, associated with Kempe Gowda's time.

  6. Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple Cave shrine, expanded 16th century

    Natural cave temple with monolithic discs in the courtyard and a winter solar alignment.

  7. Someshwara Temple, Halasuru Chola origins, Vijayanagara expansion

    Large Shiva temple with a tall gopuram and carved pillared halls. Reached by vehicle.

  8. Lalbagh Begun 1760s, Glass House 1889

    Garden started by Hyder Ali. One of the four Kempe Gowda towers stands on a rock outcrop inside.

  9. Attara Kacheri 1868

    Red Neoclassical building that held eighteen government offices, now the Karnataka High Court.

  10. Cubbon Park 1870

    Park laid out around the civic buildings of colonial Bangalore. A good place to discuss planning.

  11. Government Museum 1877

    Karnataka sculpture, inscriptions and coins in a red Neoclassical building.

  12. Vidhana Soudha Completed 1956

    Granite legislature in a neo-Dravidian style, seen from outside.

Walking routes in Bengaluru

Fort, palace and pete

About 3 hours

Bangalore Fort → Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace → Kote Venkataramana Temple → Chickpet and Avenue Road

Basavanagudi and Lalbagh

About 3 hours, short drive between clusters

Bull Temple → Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple → Lalbagh

Cubbon Park and the civic centre

About 2.5 hours

Attara Kacheri → Cubbon Park → Government Museum → Vidhana Soudha

Museums in Bengaluru

  • Government Museum, Bengaluru. Hoysala sculpture, inscriptions, coins and Harappan material.
  • Venkatappa Art Gallery. Modern Karnataka art next to the Government Museum.
  • National Gallery of Modern Art. Modern Indian art in a 20th century mansion on Palace Road.

Best time for a walk

Most of the year is comfortable. October to February is driest; heavy rain is common in September and October afternoons.

What you see on a heritage walk in Bengaluru

The pete walk starts at what remains of Bangalore Fort, crosses to Tipu Sultan's wooden summer palace with its painted arches, and passes the Kote Venkataramana Temple next door, built in the Wodeyar period around 1689. From there the lanes of Chickpet and Avenue Road show how a 16th century market plan still shapes trade. Old houses, wholesale cloth shops and small shrines line the streets.

In Basavanagudi, the Bull Temple (Dodda Basavana Gudi) holds a monolithic Nandi, and the cave temple of Gavi Gangadhareshwara has stone discs in the courtyard aligned so that the sun lights the inner shrine around Makara Sankranti in January.

The Cubbon Park route is about colonial planning: the red Attara Kacheri, the Government Museum, the State Central Library and Vidhana Soudha. Students of architecture enjoy comparing Neoclassical and the neo-Dravidian style of Vidhana Soudha.

Museums in Bengaluru

The Government Museum (1877) beside Cubbon Park has sculpture from Halebidu and other Karnataka sites, inscriptions and coins, and finds from Mohenjo-daro sent from excavations in the 1920s and 1930s. Next door, the Venkatappa Art Gallery shows modern Karnataka art. The National Gallery of Modern Art occupies Manikyavelu Mansion on Palace Road.

A museum gallery study with an archaeologist or the museum object identification lab turns these galleries into practical sessions for students.

Bengaluru heritage walk for schools and colleges

The fort and palace walk suits schools: it links to the Anglo-Mysore wars and is compact. The pete is crowded, so keep groups small and use more adults. Colleges in architecture, urban studies and history can do a fuller day across all three areas.

We plan Bengaluru walks around your group: the route, length and language are set with you. For temples, groups often add Belur, Halebidu or Somanathapura, all a long day's drive; see our Pattadakal and Aihole programme, the south India temple architecture study tour and the page on heritage sites in Karnataka.

Practical advice for groups

Bengaluru's weather is mild, but traffic is heavy. Start walks by 8 am, especially in the pete. Tipu's palace and the fort are ASI monuments; check the ASI website for timings. Temples have their own dress rules. Vidhana Soudha is a working legislature and is seen from outside unless you have permission.

Questions people ask

What are the main historical places in Bengaluru?

Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace, Bangalore Fort, the Kote Venkataramana Temple, the Bull Temple, Gavi Gangadhareshwara, the Someshwara Temple at Halasuru, Lalbagh, Attara Kacheri, the Government Museum and Vidhana Soudha.

Who founded Bengaluru?

Kempe Gowda I, a chieftain under the Vijayanagara rulers, founded the town with its mud fort and market grid in 1537. Older inscriptions show settlements in the area centuries earlier.

Is a Bengaluru heritage walk suitable for schools?

Yes. The fort and Tipu's palace route is compact and links to the Anglo-Mysore wars. The market lanes are busy, so use small groups and more adults there.

Which heritage sites can I visit near Bengaluru?

Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura, part of the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (UNESCO, 2023), and Srirangapatna and Mysuru. All need a full day by road.
